headings.text: When to use the cluster pod instead

blocks.html:
On the Kubernetes stack the inner loop does not run uvicorn inside the cluster. Instead you keep the full stack running in kind (see Set up your dev environment (Kubernetes)) and use mirrord to make your local core process handle the cluster's traffic for deployment/opendefense-rmapi. You edit code on your machine, uvicorn reloads locally, and the running cluster routes real requests to it. This is the platform repo's "Developing using mirrord" workflow.

Prerequisites

  • The platform stack up locally: task up against the opendefense-kind cluster, with opendefense-rmapi healthy in namespace opendefense-system.
  • A local checkout of the rasenmaeher repo (pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api) with its dependencies installed via Poetry — you run mirrord from that repo, not from the platform repo.
  • mirrord installed locally.

The mirrord inner loop

From the rasenmaeher repo, run your local core under uvicorn but stolen into the cluster target:

mirrord exec --steal \
  --target-namespace opendefense-system \
  --target deployment/opendefense-rmapi \
  -- bash -c 'JWT_PRIVKEY_PATH=./locadir/private/rm_jwtsign.key JWT_PUBKEY_PATH=./locadir/public poetry run uvicorn --reload --factory rasenmaeher_api.web.application:get_app'

What this does:

  • --steal intercepts traffic destined for the targeted deployment and routes it to your local process (rather than just mirroring a copy). Your laptop now answers requests that the in-cluster opendefense-rmapi would have served.
  • --target-namespace opendefense-system --target deployment/opendefense-rmapi selects the core deployment as the interception target.
  • The command after -- is your local app: poetry run uvicorn --reload --factory rasenmaeher_api.web.application:get_app, with the JWT signing key paths pointed at local files.

The loop is then:

  1. Edit rasenmaeher_api source locally.
  2. uvicorn --reload restarts your local app on save.
  3. Drive the stack as normal (UI, other components, product-integration callbacks) — requests for the core land on your local process.
  4. Watch your local terminal for logs/tracebacks instead of kubectl logs.

JWT key paths

The example sets JWT_PRIVKEY_PATH and JWT_PUBKEY_PATH to local paths (./locadir/...) so your local instance can sign/verify JWTs. Make sure those files exist locally before starting.

Not yet documented. How ./locadir/private/rm_jwtsign.key and ./locadir/public are produced for local mirrord runs — generated by the rasenmaeher repo's tooling, or copied out of the cluster — is still to be written here.

Inspecting the in-cluster deployment

While iterating it is useful to see the target you are stealing from:

kubectl get deployment opendefense-rmapi -n opendefense-system
kubectl describe deployment opendefense-rmapi -n opendefense-system
kubectl logs -n opendefense-system deployment/opendefense-rmapi   # the in-cluster pod (when not stealing)

Note the in-cluster container listens on port 8000; match your local uvicorn to the same port the cluster expects so the stolen traffic is served correctly.

Not yet documented. The local uvicorn --port / --host binding that the platform's mirrord setup expects is still to be written here (the README example omits it); it should align with the deployment's containerPort 8000.

When to use the cluster pod instead

mirrord is for the core inner loop. If you are changing manifests, Kustomize overlays, or the deploy phasing rather than core Python, do that in the platform repo and redeploy with task deploy (or task up for a fresh cluster) — see Set up your dev environment (Kubernetes) and agents.md.
